Class ColumnWriter

Namespace
ParquetNeo

Writes the values of one column of a row group. Obtain it from NextColumn(), call one of the Write… methods one or more times, then move on to the next column.

Remarks

For a required column pass only the values. For an optional column also pass one definition level per row: 0 for a null and 1 for a value, with values holding just the non-null values in order.

A nested column (a leaf below optional or repeated groups) has a definition level per entry that counts how many of its optional and repeated ancestors, and itself, are present, up to MaxDefinitionLevel: only entries at that level carry a value. A column inside a repeated group also takes a repetition level per entry, which says at which repeated ancestor the entry repeats: 0 starts a new row, and a higher level continues the row at that depth. Entries are the unit of a batch; a row can span several entries and even several batches (it ends where the next entry with repetition level 0 begins), and the first entry of a column must start a row. Pages never end in the middle of a row. The levels are checked against their ranges but not against the schema's structure: levels that no row could produce give a file readers will reject.

Values are buffered into pages of about DataPageSize bytes, which are compressed and written to the stream as they fill. Instances are not thread safe.

WriteBatch(ReadOnlySpan<decimal>, ReadOnlySpan<int>, ReadOnlySpan<int>)

Writes a DECIMAL column of any physical type (INT32, INT64, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY or BYTE_ARRAY) from decimal values. Digits are never lost: a value with more decimals than the column's scale, or more digits than its precision, is an ArgumentOutOfRangeException. A column with a scale above 28 cannot be written from a decimal.
